newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude prices edge up but wary of Brent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude prices edge up but wary of Brent.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices were a touch firmer in late Tuesday's quiet market, with outright prices erasing early gains while grade differentials firmed up a bit.
There was little news to move prices and traders spent much of the day awaiting the latest weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) status report.
Marker West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was hardly changed, with July futures ending a cent lower on the day at $8.67 and the exchange-for-physical premium still hovering around 20 cents.

Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded at discounts between 19 cents and 24 cents to WTI, continuing a firmer trend over the last few days as the arbitrage for North Sea crude to the U.S. appeared to disappear.
West Texas Sour/Midland also traded firmer, with deals at discounts around $1.65/$1.68, compared with $1.71 on Monday.

However, traders noted that the price for prompt Brent in Europe was still under pressure and it appeared that a trading house might be assembling enough Brent to ship a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) to the U.S.
"People talk about the $1.50 breakeven (WTI/Brent) level (to ship crude trans-Atlantic). But it is completely different economics when you are looking at a VLCC," said one crude trader.
Dated Brent traded at a 70 cents discount to July Brent on Tuesday, down from a previous deal for the same June 17-19 loading dates of 62 cents under on Monday.
"The key to today's market was that minus 70 number. That really showed people there was some further downside," said another Texas trader.

The July/July WTI/Brent spread, while still down at $1.15 from levels around $1.70 and higher earlier in the month, looks much wider when factoring in the prompt discount and spreading shipping costs.

In the API report, crude stocks rose only marginally last week as imports remained high at around 8.4 million barrels a day. Gasoline continued to build as production remained up at near record levels and the year-on-year deficit was halved to around three million barrels.
